title: Optimise network performance and security, and choose load balancing
learningObjective: Recommend solutions to optimise network performance and security, and a load-balancing and routing solution.
foundation: Fast networks keep data close (same region, zone or rack) and take short, private paths.
Secure networks use layers: perimeter (DDoS, WAF), central firewall, segmentation (NSGs), and private access to services.
Load balancing has a simple rule: global or regional, web or any protocol.
engineer: Performance: accelerated networking (SR-IOV) on supported VM sizes; proximity placement groups and same-zone placement for chatty tiers; choose regions close to users; Front Door or CDN for edge delivery; ExpressRoute (FastPath, Global Reach) for hybrid latency and throughput; Traffic Manager performance routing; VNet peering instead of gateways between VNets; private endpoints for low-latency private access.

Security layers: DDoS Network Protection (or IP Protection) for public IPs; Web Application Firewall on Front Door or Application Gateway; Azure Firewall (Standard: L3–L7 rules, FQDN filtering, threat intelligence; Premium: TLS inspection, IDPS, URL filtering) in the hub; NSGs and ASGs for micro-segmentation; Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules for organisation-wide guardrails; Private Link and disabled public network access for PaaS; Bastion for admin access; Network Watcher and VNet flow logs for visibility; Zero Trust principles.

Load balancing and routing decision: global + HTTP(S) → Front Door; global + any protocol → Traffic Manager (DNS-based) or cross-region Load Balancer; regional + HTTP(S) → Application Gateway (path routing, TLS termination, WAF) or Application Gateway for Containers; regional + TCP/UDP → Load Balancer (internal or public, HA ports for NVAs, Gateway Load Balancer for inline appliances). Combine them: Front Door → Application Gateway → internal Load Balancer.

animation.caption: Choose performance features, security layers and the right load balancer.

example.title: A secure, fast global storefront
body: Front Door Premium with WAF fronts the site; each region has Application Gateway routing /api and /static, and an internal Load Balancer for the order service. DDoS Network Protection covers the public IPs.

Azure Firewall Premium inspects outbound TLS; spokes are segmented with NSGs and ASGs; PaaS services use private endpoints. Latency-sensitive trading VMs use accelerated networking in a proximity placement group.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: VM > Networking > Accelerated networking; Proximity placement groups.
Azure Firewall policy: Premium features (TLS inspection, IDPS).
DDoS protection plan: associate with VNets.
Front Door / Application Gateway: WAF policy.

troubleshooting.symptom: Latency between app and database VMs is inconsistent.
troubleshooting.cause: VMs placed far apart; no accelerated networking.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a proximity placement group and enable accelerated networking.

troubleshooting.symptom: A website is hit by SQL injection attempts.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable WAF managed rules on Front Door or Application Gateway.

comparisons.difference: Firewall: central, stateful, FQDN and threat intelligence; NSG: distributed L3/L4 allow/deny per subnet or NIC.
Front Door proxies HTTP(S) with WAF and caching; Traffic Manager only answers DNS.

misconceptions.reality: Defence in depth: DDoS, WAF, firewall, NSGs, private access.
It works at DNS level; clients connect directly to endpoints.

architectureDecisions: Accelerated networking and PPGs for latency-sensitive tiers.
Layer DDoS + WAF + Firewall + NSGs + Private Link.
Pick the load balancer by global/regional and HTTP/any.

walkthrough.subtitle: Make traffic fast and safe, and send it to the right place.

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Slow, exposed, or both
body: Trading VMs need microseconds, the website faces attacks, and traffic must reach the right backend.

steps.label: Fast
steps.title: Keep it close and offload work
body: Proximity placement groups keep VMs physically close; accelerated networking offloads packet processing to hardware. Choose regions near users and cache at the edge.

steps.label: Secure
steps.title: Defence in layers
body: DDoS Protection on public IPs, a web application firewall on the entry point, Azure Firewall in the hub for central filtering, NSGs and ASGs for segmentation, and Private Link so PaaS services stay off the internet.

steps.label: Route
steps.title: Two questions pick the balancer
body: Global or regional? Web (HTTP/S) or any protocol? Global + web: Front Door. Regional + web: Application Gateway. Regional + any: Load Balancer. Global + any: Traffic Manager.

callout.text: Designs often chain them: Front Door → Application Gateway → internal Load Balancer.
